summary:
Beyond Hotspot Detection – Intelligent Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Using Fire Behaviour Prediction

Wildfires cause serious damage to forests, wildlife, and communities. Satellite systems like MODIS and VIIRS help detect active fires, but combining their data can provide better monitoring.

This project aims to harmonize hotspot data from both satellites using NASA FIRMS. It will match observations based on location and time, group nearby detections into possible fire events, and analyse how these events change over time.

A key feature, Fire Behaviour Continuity Analysis (FBCA), will classify fires as expanding, stable, fragmented, or declining. A Sensor Disagreement Intelligence System will investigate differences between satellite observations. The project will also introduce a Fire Observation Reliability Score based on confidence, satellite agreement, and temporal consistency.

Finally, an interactive dashboard will display hotspots, fire progression, and satellite differences, helping improve wildfire monitoring and environmental decision-making.
details: Our project combines MODIS and VIIRS satellite data to improve wildfire monitoring. It matches hotspots, groups them into fire events, and analyses their behaviour over time. It identifies expanding, stable, fragmented, or declining fires and investigates differences between satellite observations. Python, Pandas, GeoPandas, Matplotlib, and NASA FIRMS data are used. Its creative features include fire behaviour analysis and a reliability score. We considered accuracy, spatial resolution, detection time, and confidence levels. The goal is to support better fire monitoring and disaster management.
